audit_items.proof_trace: The validate() method only checks config_name validity but never enforces fork epoch ordering. The phase_at_epoch() method at L920-926 relies on fork_epochs() yielding epochs in chronological order via enum_iterator iteration, but nothing prevents deserialized Config from having misordered epochs (e.g., ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH=100 < DENEB_FORK_EPOCH=200), causing phase_at_epoch to return wrong phase for intermediate epochs.
audit_items.attack_scenario: An attacker provides a malicious config.yaml with ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH=100 < DENEB_FORK_EPOCH=200. At epoch 150, phase_at_epoch(150) would return Electra (last phase <= 150) instead of the spec-mandated Deneb, causing state transitions to use wrong fork logic, potentially accepting invalid blocks or rejecting valid ones, leading to consensus split.
